domain_restrictions: n is an integer with n > 1
a is an integer satisfying 0 <= a <= n-1
the expression a/n is a rational number in the interval from 0 up to but not including 1
E_n(x) and H_n are defined (and yield numbers comparable with <= and =) for x = a/n and for index n
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For every integer n with n > 1 and every integer a with 0 <= a <= n-1, the inequality E_n(a divided by n) <= H_n minus 1 holds. Moreover, E_n(a divided by n) equals H_n minus 1 if and only if a equals n minus 1.

variables.name: n
variables.role: outer universally quantified parameter indexing E and H

variables.domain: all integers with 0 <= a <= n-1 (depending on n)
variables.name: a
variables.role: inner universally quantified parameter controlling the argument a/n

witness_dependencies: none (no existential quantifiers); the equality condition depends only on the universally quantified variable a and the universally quantified parameter n

statement_nl: For every integer n>1 and every integer a with 0 <= a <= n-1, one has E_n(a/n) <= H_n - 1, and equality holds if and only if a = n-1.
